title: Trailing zeros in 100!
prompt: How many trailing zeros does 100! (one hundred factorial) have?
A trailing zero is a zero at the end of a number before the decimal point. For example, 7,000 has three trailing zeros.
hints: A trailing zero requires a factor of 10 = 2 × 5. How do the counts of factors of 2 and factors of 5 compare in 100!?
Factors of 2 vastly outnumber factors of 5 in any factorial. So the number of trailing zeros equals the total count of times 5 appears as a factor across all numbers from 1 to 100.
Count multiples of 5 up to 100 (each contributes one factor of 5), then multiples of 25 (each contributes an extra one). What do you get?
solution_lede:
Every trailing zero comes from a factor of 10 = 2 × 5. In 100!, factors of 2 are plentiful — every even number contributes at least one. Factors of 5 are the bottleneck: they're rarer, so the count of 5s determines the number of trailing zeros.

To count all factors of 5 in 100!, use Legendre's formula: sum ⌊100/5⌋ + ⌊100/25⌋ + ⌊100/125⌋ + …

⌊100/5⌋ = 20 (numbers divisible by 5)
⌊100/25⌋ = 4 (numbers divisible by 25, each with an extra factor of 5: 25, 50, 75, 100)
⌊100/125⌋ = 0

Total: 20 + 4 = 24 trailing zeros.

solution_steps.body: Each trailing zero needs one factor of 2 and one factor of 5. Factors of 2 are abundant; count factors of 5.
Multiples of 5 up to 100: 5, 10, 15, …, 100. That's ⌊100/5⌋ = 20, contributing 20 factors of 5.
Multiples of 25 up to 100: 25, 50, 75, 100. That's ⌊100/25⌋ = 4, each contributing one extra factor of 5.
Total factors of 5: 20 + 4 = 24. Therefore 100! ends in exactly 24 zeros.
